title: Concavity bound on sampled payoff against a mixed column
statement:
Let $f:\bbr\times\bbr\to\bbr$ be a payoff function taking values in $[0,1]$, and let $x:[M]\to\bbr$ and $y:[N]\to\bbr$ be finite families of row and column points. Fix a row index $i$ and a mixed column strategy $q$, whose weights $q_j\ge 0$ sum to $1$. Suppose $Y\subseteq\bbr$ contains every $y_j$ and the section $y'\mapsto f(x_i,y')$ is concave on $Y$. Then the expected payoff of pure row $i$ against $q$ in the sampled game is at most the value of $f$ at the $q$-averaged column point:
\[
  \sum_{j} f(x_i,y_j)\, q_j \;\le\; f\!\left(x_i,\; \sum_{j} q_j\, y_j\right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: q is a mixed strategy: weights nonnegative and summing to 1
the section f(x_i, ·) is concave on Y
every column point y_j lies in Y
replaced:
If $f(x_i,\cdot)$ is concave on $Y$ and every $y_j \in Y$, then for any mixed
column strategy $q \in \Delta_N$,
\[
  \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(\mathrm{sampledGame},\,i,\,q)
  \;\leq\;
  f\!\left(x_i,\; \sum_j q_j\,y_j\right).
\]
